preconditions.description: The length of the string n is between 1 and 10^5 inclusive.
The number of bracket types k is between 1 and n inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(s) == n and all(1 <= abs(x) <= k for x in s)
preconditions.description: The initial string s has length n, and every element is an integer with absolute value between 1 and k.
The number of queries q is between 1 and 10^5 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all((1 <= i <= n and 1 <= abs(t) <= k) if type == 1 else (1 <= l <= r <= n) for (type, i, t, l, r) in queries_parsed)
preconditions.description: For type 1 queries, index i is valid and t is a valid bracket type; for type 2 queries, l and r are valid indices with l <= r.

postconditions.expression: len(output_lines) == len([q for q in queries_parsed if q[0] == 2])
postconditions.description: The number of output lines equals the number of type 2 queries.

postconditions.expression: all((line.lower() == 'yes' and is_correct_bracket_sequence(current_s[l-1:r])) or (line.lower() == 'no' and not is_correct_bracket_sequence(current_s[l-1:r])) for line, (q_type, i, t, l, r) in zip(output_lines, [q for q in queries_parsed if q[0] == 2]))
postconditions.description: For each type 2 query (l, r), the output is 'Yes' if and only if the substring from l to r in the current state of the string is a correct bracket sequence, and 'No' otherwise.
